recipes.name: Clone of a Pretzel Dip
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup spicy brown mustard (such as Gulden's®)
3 tablespoons red raspberry preserves (such as Smucker's®)

steps.text: In a bowl, thoroughly combine the spicy brown mustard, honey, raspberry preserves, and mustard seeds. Serve in a dip bowl surrounded by pretzels. Store refrigerated. Dip will thicken when cold.

raw_recipe.headline: Clone of a Pretzel Dip
raw_recipe.description: Spicy brown mustard, mustard seeds, honey, and raspberry preserves mix it up to make an easy dip for pretzels.

review.reviewBody: I made this months ago when shorecook first shared this recipe. It's really tasty. I served it with Snyder's pretzels and my family at the whole bowlful. I commented back then that I think this would make a great glaze for chicken or pork, too. Kind of sweet and sour-y.

I followed this recipe as written, but the dip is really runny and does not stick to the pretzel. Any ideas on a good way to thicken it up? The flavor is great, but the consistency leaves a lot to be desired. ***UPDATE ON THE RUNNINESS ISSUE**** 12/1/15 This was driving me crazy..... so I took 3 sheets of gelatin, soaked in cold water for 5 mins and then shook out the excess water when removing the sheets. Microwaved for 5 sec and then added to my runny dip and let set for about 1/2 hour - it was perfect!

This was so good that I wanted to just drink it! And don't bother making 1/2 the batch because you will be back in the kitchen making more within minutes! This doesn't make a large amount, so just go for it! I didn't have mustards seeds so I omitted that. I also added a few rings of jarred jalapeno for some heat. I mashed them and added it to the other ingredients. This does thicken up when chilled for a few hours...if you can wait that long! I'll be using this dip for soft pretzels next time. Thanks Shorecook!

I made this to dip pretzels dogs in as many reviewers suggested this dipping sauce. However, if I make it again, I would cut back on the sweet (honey) and make it more (savory) mustardy. I was afraid it would be too sweet and it was, I even added mustard powder to combat the sweetness. :/ It makes quite a bit of dipping sauce, so half a recipe would be plenty. Now...what to do with a surplus of sauce that I really didn't love?

This was really good. I substituted hot pepper jelly for the raspberry preserves. We rarely use fruit spreads, so I was trying to find uses for a jar that's been hanging around and wasn't sure if it would work in this. I read through some reviews and saw that it had worked for another person so I gave it a shot. I'm so glad I did. This had a slight drip to it before chilling, but was not runny for me. It did thicken more after refrigerating. I still have more jelly and honey to use up so we'll be making this again.
I made this with sugar free raspberry preserves and sugar free honey because my husband has diabetes, he liked it.

I usually purchase Rothchilds raspberry honey mustard pretzel dip. This is very close to that recipe. I put this mixture over meatballs in a crackpot. It is fabulous. It is very simple to make. I have subistuted boysenberry jam for the raspberry and it is just as good.
Good and spicy with a hint of sweetness! I think it’s actually a bit too spicy for me so next time I would just use regular Dijon mustard

Oh wow, this tastes just like those sample dips at the gourmet grocery stores. I had no idea how simple it would be to mix up. I actually had near all of the ingredients in the house. The only thing I didn't have was the mustard seed and it was fine without it. I also had to substitute strawberry jam for the raspberry, but it was no big deal. I scaled the recipe back to 4 servings, but it came out to be more like 2. This was an interesting recipe, to use up a too large bag of pretzels I bought for another recipe.

I will be making it for Christmas. I did discover that there is a discrepancy between the written recipe and the shopping list that might clear up problems for some people. The recipe calls for raspberry preserves however, the shopping list calls for raspberry jam. This is probably the reason that some people had trouble with the recipe. Preserves would give the dip a better thicker dip consistency. I will use preserves. Rated it high because it sounds so yummy.

Loved this! I used Trader Joe's Spicy Brown Mustard and otherwise followed the recipe. It wasn't quite spicy enough for me, so I added another little bit of mustard that I have that has a little more bite to it. This is excellent! I made it to serve alongside some pork chops that we had for dinner. I can't wait to share this with friends! Thank you so much, SHORECOOK!
This dip is amazing. It's tangy, sweet and spicy, with a beautiful, rich consistency. Try it with homemade chicken fritters!
Stonewall kitchen ? I need someone to make the honey mustard pretzel dip from there!! Lol! Can’t wait to try this one!

Served with Jan's Pretzel Dogs. 
Wonderful ~ will make it again.
Took this and pretzel dogs to a football party. Everyone loved it.

I loved it as shown in recipe. My kids thought it was a little too mustardy. Next time I'll probably slightly reduce the mustard. I did add a bit more jam and honey after initial tasting to please the kids. Don't think I'll need to buy it online in the future
Loved it! No need for any changes.
I used Dijon mustard which was all I had. Whoa! Too strong mustard flavor. Added more honey. Good thing I only made half the recipe.
This is great dip and sooo easy!! Served with Jan's pretzel hot dogs and was delicious!
Great flavor. I didnt have mustard seeds so I omitted that.
